master.title: Ukraine's official commitment not to join NATO would be substantial step toward addressing Russia's concerns - Kremlin; Russia has nothing to de-escalate in Ukraine, West should do so - diplomat
master.content:
Putin-Scholz talks to address Ukraine, security guarantees, Nord Stream 2 - Peskov

MOSCOW. Feb 14 (Interfax) - The Kremlin is expecting the upcoming talks between Russian President Vladimir Putin and German Federal Chancellor Olaf Scholz to address the Ukraine situation, security guarantees, and the Nord Stream 2 gas pipeline project.

Journalists asked Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov on Monday whether the talks would put emphasis on the Ukraine crisis, the security guarantees or the Nord Stream 2 project. "All of the above," Peskov said.

Putin, Scholz to give joint press conference after Moscow talks - Peskov

MOSCOW. Feb 14 (Interfax) - Russian President Vladimir Putin will give a joint press conference after talks in Moscow on Tuesday, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.

"He [Scholz] will have a meeting with Putin, followed by a working breakfast and a joint press conference," Peskov said at a press briefing on Monday.

The Kremlin is expecting the talks to address the Ukraine situation, security guarantees, and the Nord Stream 2 project, he said.

As reported earlier, Putin and Scholz will hold talks in Moscow on February 15.

Ukraine's official commitment not to join NATO would be substantial step toward addressing Russia's concerns - Kremlin

MOSCOW. Feb 14 (Interfax) - Ukraine's official commitment not to join NATO would be a substantial contribution to addressing Russia's concerns, Russian presidential press secretary Dmitry Peskov said.

"Definitely, Ukraine's confirmed and somehow formalized commitment to abandon its idea to join NATO would certainly be a step that would substantially promote the formulation of a more meaningful response to Russia's concerns," Peskov told journalists on Monday, in reply to specific question.

Russian forces strictly comply with protocols whenever foreign ships trespass in Russian territorial waters - Peskov

MOSCOW. Feb 14 (Interfax) - Russian forces strictly comply with protocols whenever foreign ships trespass in Russian territorial waters, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.

Journalists asked Peskov on Monday to comment on a statement by a Russian General Staff officer who said that Russia was ready to strike on foreign ships and subs trespassing in its territorial waters.

"There is a specific protocol which is activated whenever foreign ships, either surface ships or submarines, trespass into Russian territorial waters. Of course, our servicemen responsible for the protection of our border and the security of our country strictly comply with these protocols," Peskov said.

Russia has nothing to de-escalate in Ukraine, West should do so - diplomat

MOSCOW. Feb 14 (Interfax) - Russia has nothing to de-escalate in Ukraine, and it is actually the West that should do this by prompting Kyiv to abide by the Minsk Agreements, Oleg Postnikov, deputy director of the Russian Foreign Ministry's Department for Nonproliferation and Arms Control, said on Monday.

"The subjects on which the United States has manifested its desire to have a businesslike conversation have been removed from context of a package deal, and have been made conditional upon our provisional steps toward a de-escalation of the situation in and around Ukraine. We have nothing to de-escalate there. It's the West that should ensure de-escalation, primarily by having their proteges in Kyiv strictly and comprehensively abide by the Minsk Package of Measures," Postnikov said at a roundtable conference at the Federation Council.

West's response to Russia's security guarantee proposals disappointing - Russian diplomat

MOSCOW. Feb 14 (Interfax) - The West's reaction to Russia's proposals on security guarantees is disappointing and does not show any desire to establish a constructive dialogue, Oleg Postnikov, deputy director of the Russian Foreign Ministry's Department for Nonproliferation and Arms Control, said on Monday.

"The collective West's reaction cannot be described other than disappointing. It does not show any desire to constructively address our key demands on NATO's non-enlargement and on the configuration of the alliance's forces. The principle of non-divisible security, which is key for us, has been circumvented," Postnikov said at a roundtable at the Russian Federation Council on Monday.

Moscow won't allow West to ignore its proposals on security guarantees - Russian Foreign Ministry

MOSCOW. Feb 14 (Interfax) - Russia will not allow its proposals on security guarantees "to be swept under the rug," Oleg Postnikov, deputy director of the Russian Foreign Ministry's Department for Nonproliferation and Arms Control, said on Monday.

"We have increasingly more questions as to whether our Western counterparts are capable of reaching any agreements at all, but there is absolutely no alternative for us to continuing to try to bring them closer to our approaches, clarify our position, and not allow the concerns we have declared to be swept under the rug," Postnikov said at a roundtable at the Federation Council.

Moscow analyzing U.S., NATO response to its security guarantee proposals - Foreign Ministry

MOSCOW. Feb 14 (Interfax) - Moscow is continuing to analyze answers to its security guarantee proposals from the United States and NATO and to consider further actions, Deputy Director of the Russian Foreign Ministry's Non-Proliferation and Arms Control Department Oleg Postnikov said on Monday.

"We are continuing to analyze the U.S. and NATO considerations and are elaborating our stance on further actions. The Western capitals must not be allowed to ignore our lawful concern about their interpretation of the indivisible security principle, which, by the way, they have signed up to multiple times," Postnikov said at a Federation Council roundtable.

U.S. does not want to stop NATO enlargement, reconfigure forces in Europe - General Staff

MOSCOW. Feb 14 (Interfax) - The United States does not support Russia's call for the non-enlargement of NATO and does not want to reconfigure the forces stationed in Europe, the Russian General Staff said.

"An analysis of the U.S. document suggests that the United States is not going to hold negotiations on terms of the Russian draft agreement," deputy head of the Russian General Staff's Main Operational Directorate Stanislav Gadzhimagomedov said at a Federation Council roundtable on Monday.

"Washington will stay committed to its values and obligations, will continue to support NATO's Open Doors Policy, and will be defending - I'm quoting the U.S. stance - the inherent right of every state to choose and use the methods of provision of its security, including alliances," he said.

"There are no plans to change the configuration of U.S. and NATO forces in Europe, which is allegedly limited, proportionate and fully compliant with obligations," Gadzhimagomedov said.

U.S., NATO seek to create bridgehead for their troops in Ukraine - Russian General Staff

MOSCOW. Feb 14 (Interfax) - The United States and other Western nations are building a bridgehead for their troops in Ukraine and are provoking Kyiv to solve the problem of Donbas and Crimea by force, deputy head of the Russian General Staff's Main Operational Directorate Stanislav Gadzhimagomedov said on Monday.

"The West is continuing to transform Ukraine into a state hostile towards us, what our supreme commander-in-chief has described as an 'anti-Russia', by creating a bridgehead for the deployment of NATO troops on its territory," Gadzhimagomedov said at a roundtable in the Federation Council.

"Foreign political and military support is provoking Kyiv to retake control of Donbas and, later on, of Crimea through a military scenario," he said.

"Washington has been speculating on the admission of Ukraine and Georgia to the North Atlantic Alliance so that it could continue to artificially maintain military-political tensions," Gadzhimagomedov said.

"The NATO naval activity in the Black Sea and the Baltic Sea has markedly intensified in the recent period in the close vicinity of the Russian Federation," he said.

The recent talks with the British defense secretary touched upon the entry of Russian territorial waters by the British destroyer Defender, Gadzhimagomedov said.

"He said directly that they viewed Crimea as the territory of Ukraine and therefore entered Ukrainian territorial waters. He said they have done that before and will continue to do so in the future," he said.

The Russian Defense Ministry said on June 23, 2021, that the Russian military and border guards fired warning shots along the course of the British destroyer Defender that breached the Russian border off Cape Fiolent, Crimea, in the Black Sea.

U.S. trying to stall Russian security initiatives - Russian General Staff

MOSCOW. Feb 14 (Interfax) - Washington has been stalling Moscow's security initiatives, deputy head of the Russian General Staff's Main Operational Directorate Stanislav Gadzhimagomedov said on Monday.

"The U.S. posture [...] indicates a desire to follow the scenario repeatedly used by the Americans before, and aimed at stalling Russian initiatives through drawing Russia into long talks on issues which are not essential to the Americans, either in the area of Russia-U.S. strategic stability dialogue or in multilateral formats, such as the NATO-Russia Council or the OSCE," Gadzhimagomedov said at a Federation Council meeting.

"An analysis of the U.S. document shows that the United States is not going to conduct negotiations on the basis of the Russian draft agreement," he said.

"Washington will stay committed to its values and obligations, will continue to support NATO's Open Doors Policy, and will be defending - I'm quoting the U.S. stance - the inherent right of every state to choose and use the methods for the provision of its security, including alliances," Gadzhimagomedov said.

U.S. seeking Russia's, China's nuclear disarmament while not disarming itself - Russian diplomat

MOSCOW. Feb 14 (Interfax) - The United States is seeking to ensure the nuclear disarmament of only Russia and China, which is unacceptable to Moscow, Oleg Postnikov, deputy director of the Russian Foreign Ministry's Department for Nonproliferation and Arms Control, said on Monday.

"A number of non-nuclear states are seeking an accelerated nuclear disarmament while completely ignoring international geopolitical realities," Postnikov said at a roundtable conference at the Russian Federation Council on Monday.

"What's interesting is that the Americans don't mind playing along with that sentiment, but in such a way as to ultimately make Russia and China the object of disarmament, while staying aside of this itself. Certainly, this is absolutely unacceptable to us," he said.

Russia must get security guarantees from U.S., NATO amid tensions over Ukraine crisis - Russian military official

MOSCOW. Feb 14 (Interfax) - Agreements between Russia, the United States, and NATO on security guarantees would be of substantial significance amid current tensions in their relations against the backdrop of the situation in and around Ukraine, Stanislav Gadzhimagomedov, deputy chief of the Main Operational Directorate of the Russian Armed Forces General Staff, said on Monday.

"In the current situation, amid the deterioration of relations between Russia and the collective West against the backdrop of the crisis in Ukraine, efforts should be concentrated on obtaining security guarantees from the U.S. and NATO," Gadzhimagomedov said.

However, the negotiations held to date and the replies that Russia has received from the U.S. and NATO show no prospects for concluding such agreements thus far, he said.

U.S. plans to deploy intermediate-range, shorter-range missiles by 2028 in Asia Pacific to deter Russia, China - Russian General Staff official

MOSCOW. Feb 14 (Interfax) - The United States will deploy intermediate-range and shorter-range missiles in the Asia Pacific region by 2028 to deter Russia and China, Stanislav Gadzhimagomedov, deputy chief of the Main Operational Directorate of the Russian Armed Forces General Staff, said on Monday.

"To back up its plans militarily, the White House intends to deploy intermediate-range and shorter range missiles in the Asia Pacific region by 2028," Gadzhimagomadov said at a roundtable at the Russian Federation Council.

The U.S. is planning to allot over $7 billion for a regional Russia and China deterrence program in 2022, he said.

"Along with this, Japan keeps hoping for Russia's Kuril Islands, and the likelihood of a conflict in the Korean Peninsula, including with the use of nuclear weapons, cannot be ruled out," Gadzhimagomedov said.

Russia ready to strike on ships that violate its borders - General Staff

MOSCOW. Feb 14 (Interfax) - Russia is ready to strike on trespassers of its sea border; however, such decisions are made at the top level, deputy head of the Russian General Staff's Main Operational Directorate Stanislav Gadzhimagomedov said on Monday.

"We are always prepared [...] But the thing is that such decisions are made exclusively at the top level," Gadzhimagomedov said at a roundtable in the Federation Council, when asked whether the Russian army was ready to fire at trespassers in cases similar to Saturday's incident where a U.S. sub was spotted in Russian territorial waters.

Russia's Black Sea Fleet naval aviation, anti-submarine ships conduct exercise to search for mock enemy sub

MOSCOW. Feb 14 (Interfax) - Pilots of a separate combined air regiment of naval aviation and crews of anti-submarine ships of Russia's Black Sea Fleet have held a joint exercise practicing the search for and tracking of a mock enemy submarine, the fleet's press service said on Monday.

"Beriev Be-12 amphibious aircraft and Kamov Ka-27PL helicopters were involved in the exercise. Their crews, in interaction with small anti-submarine ships, carried out a joint search for a submarine using radio hydroacoustic buoys and other hydroacoustic means," the statement said.

A submarine of the Black Sea Fleet acted as a mock enemy to create a real tactical situation.

The main tasks practiced during the exercise by naval pilots and ships of the Black Sea Fleet were joint actions to search for, continuously track and conditionally destroy a submarine at long and short ranges, as well as to organize the continuous exchange of data on the maneuvering of an underwater target, the press service said.

Russian troops to leave Belarus at end of exercise, relevant decision made together with Putin - Lukashenko

MINSK. Feb 14 (Interfax) - Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko has said when the Russian troops, deployed to Belarus for the Union Resolve 2022 exercise, will go home.

"They will leave when the Russian president and I decide to do it and when the exercise is over. The decision will be made by us: this is our territory," the Belarusian state-run news agency BelTA quoted Lukashenko as saying at a meeting with Ukrainian politician Oleksandr Moroz in Minsk on Monday.

"Look what the Americans are doing: they are deploying thousands of troops to our border, directly to Poland and the Baltic countries. The UK and other European countries are deploying troops. There is a reasonable question when those troops might be withdrawn. They do not say that, but they are pressuring us," Lukashenko said.

Russia and Belarus are conducting a preparedness check of the Union State's rapid response forces. Troops were redeployed and a contingent was formed at the first stage, which ended on February 9, and the Union Resolve 2022 exercise is taking place at the second stage, between February 10 and February 20.

The exercise involves Belarusian forces and units of the Russian Eastern Military District, Aerospace Forces and Airborne Forces. S-400 Triumph long-range air defense missile systems, Pantsir-S short-range air defense missile systems, Sukhoi Su-35 fourth-generation multirole fighter jets, and Su-25SM attack planes were deployed from Russia to Belarus.

candidate.title: News reports in Russia: Lavrov presenting proposals to Putin on Russia's response to U.S. reply on security guarantees; Scholz says no reasons for Russia's military activity near Ukrainian border
candidate.content:
Lavrov presenting proposals to Putin on Russia's response to U.S. reply on security guarantees

MOSCOW. Feb 14 (Interfax) - Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov is presenting a report to President Vladimir Putin on proposals regarding Russia's response to a reply from the United States concerning security guarantee proposals.

"You and I agreed today that the Russian Foreign Ministry would present its considerations regarding the replies that we have received to our proposals forwarded previously to our American counterparts in Washington and the North Atlantic alliance counterparts in Brussels," Putin said at a meeting with Lavrov on Monday.

The matter concerns security in Europe and a response to Russia's concerns related to "what we see as NATO's unending and very dangerous enlargement eastward, now involving former Soviet republics, including Ukraine," he said.

"I know that such analysis has been done, and you've also worked together with colleagues from other agencies and ministries, and certainly, I'd like also to listen to your analysis and your proposals concerning a response to the replies from Washington and Brussels," he said.

Lavrov describes replies to Russia's request regarding indivisible security interpretation as unsatisfactory

MOSCOW. Feb 14 (Interfax) - The responses received by Russia following its request regarding the interpretation of the principle of indivisible security are unsatisfactory, and Moscow will continue seeking a specific reaction from each country at the national level, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said.

"The replies that I have received are unsatisfactory. None of my counterparts have responded to my direct message. We have received two small pieces of paper: one from NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg and the other from EU diplomacy chief Josep Borrell. They say: 'don't worry, it's necessary to continue dialogue, the main thing you should do is to ensure de-escalation around Ukraine'," Lavrov said at a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Monday.

"I think this precisely neglects the norm that was entrenched at the highest level whereby no organization may see itself as the chief and dominant in the Euro-Atlantic," and this is why "we will continue to seek a concrete reaction from every country since all the documents I am now reporting about were signed in a national capacity, and in that same national capacity [every nation] must answer for their content and for their obligations under those documents," Lavrov said.

There is chance to agree with U.S., NATO on key proposals on security guarantees - Lavrov

MOSCOW. Feb 14 (Interfax) - Russia is unwilling to talk endlessly with the United States and NATO on key security issues of concern to Moscow, but there is a chance to reach agreements, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said.

"We have said more than once that we warn against endless conversations on issues that need to be resolved today, but still, probably as the foreign minister, I should say that there is always a chance," Lavrov said at a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Russia, the U.S., and France have recently had contacts at the top level, and Moscow visits by German Chancellor Olaf Scholz and Polish Foreign Minister Zbigniew Rau on February 15, and by his Italian counterpart Luigi di Maio on February 16 are scheduled, the foreign minister said.

"Our consistent explanatory work and commitment to clarify our truth while being willing to listen to some serious counter-arguments [...], I think our possibilities are far from being exhausted. Of course, they [talks] should not last forever, but at this stage I would suggest that they should continue and be intensified," the minister said.

Russia will seek responses from the U.S. to the questions that have been asked, including on NATO's non-enlargement and the principle of indivisible security, Lavrov said.

Russian ruble, equities up sharply on statements by Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov

MOSCOW. Feb 14 (Interfax) - The Russian ruble and equities, which were in decline at the start of trading on Monday, rose sharply on statements made by Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov about Russia's willingness to continue dialogue with the West, which were also backed by Russian President Vladimir Putin.

In just a few minutes, the U.S. dollar exchange rate dropped by more than 1 ruble - from a little over 77 rubles/$1 to 76 rubles/$1, while the euro was also down by 1 ruble - from 87.1 rubles/$1 to 86.1 RUR/$1. Meanwhile, the MOEX Russia stock index, which had been down more than 5% in early trading, pared losses to little more than 1%, returning to the threshold of 3,500 points. As of 15:49 p.m. the MOEX stood at 3501.16 points (-1.28%), while the RTS was down 1.55% at 1447.28.

Lavrov, Shoigu statements could defuse Europe tensions - Karasin

MOSCOW. Feb 14 (Interfax) - Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov emphasizing the need to continue talks with the United States, and Defense Minister Sergei Shoigu saying that the military exercises will be over soon should help reduce tensions in Europe, Grigory Karasin, head of the foreign affairs committee in the Federation Council, said.

"Naturally, that's what we are hoping for, but we shall see how our partners will behave themselves," Karasin told Interfax on Monday.

The Russian leadership is serious about what is going on around it, verifying every step to pacify the public, he said.

"I think this responsible and serious approach was in fact reflected in the speeches of our two statesmen in their report to the president," Karasin said.

Scholz says no reasons for Russia's military activity near Ukrainian border

KYIV. Feb 14 (Interfax) - Russia's military activity near the border with Ukraine is unfounded, German Chancellor Olaf Scholz said.

"Russia's military activity is unfounded in our view, there are no logical reasons for this build-up of military potential," Scholz said at a press conference following talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Kyiv on Monday.

Ukraine's NATO membership currently not on agenda - Scholz

KYIV. Feb 14 (Interfax) - Ukraine's membership in NATO is irrelevant at the moment, German Chancellor Olaf Scholz said.

"As regards [Ukraine's] membership of the alliance, it is irrelevant now. Therefore, it is somewhat strange that the Russian government has turned an issue that is currently not on the agenda into a subject of major political debate," Scholz said at a press conference following negotiations with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Kyiv on Monday.

Ukraine and Germany differ on Nord Stream 2 - Zelensky after talks with Scholz

KYIV. Feb 14 (Interfax) - Kyiv and Berlin pursue different approaches to the Nord Stream 2 gas pipeline project, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said after a meeting with German Chancellor Olaf Scholz.

"We have discussed security risks related to Nord Stream 2. And here we have certain disagreements in assessing them. I reminded [the German chancellor] that our position remains unchanged and we look at Nord Stream 2 today exclusively through the prism of energy threats and security threats facing us and the region. We clearly understand that it is a geopolitical weapon. That's why Ukraine is demanding energy guarantees and security guarantees," Zelensky said at a joint press conference with Scholz in Kyiv on Monday.

The Ukrainian president said he invited the German chancellor to start a joint strategic dialogue in the energy sector.

Zelensky after talks with Scholz: we expect to agree to hold Normandy Four summit in near future

KYIV. Feb 14 (Interfax) - Kyiv expects an agreement to be reached on holding a meeting of the leaders of the Normandy Four countries (Ukraine, Germany, France, and Russia) in the near future, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said after talks with German Chancellor Olaf Scholz.

"We have discussed the latest steps as part of the peaceful settlement process... We expect that we will be able to hold the next talks and to agree on a summit of the Normandy Four leaders in the near future," Zelensky said at a joint press conference with Scholz in Kyiv on Monday.

Kyiv to interpret Russian Duma's adoption of resolutions recognizing DPR, LPR as rejection of Minsk accords

KYIV. Feb 14 (Interfax) - Kyiv will interpret the possible adoption by the Russian State Duma of resolutions on any format of recognizing the self-proclaimed Donetsk (DPR) and Luhansk (LPR) People's Republics as Russia's rejection of the Minsk Agreements, Mykhailo Podolyak, an advisor to the head of the Office of the Ukrainian President, told reporters.

"Not only is all this absent from the Minsk accords, but it contravenes them," Podolyak said.

At the same time, "all participants in the many-sided negotiating efforts to end the war in Donbas recognize the Minsk documents as the fundamental path toward achieving peace. Statements to this effect have also been heard from Russia many times as the official position of this state," he said.

United Russia party MPs earlier proposed that the draft appeal to the president on recognizing the DPR and the LPR submitted earlier by the Communist Party faction be forwarded to the Russian Foreign Ministry for consultations.

The draft resolution published on the Duma database on Monday proposes holding "consultations with the Russian Foreign Ministry on the State Duma's draft appeal to Russian President Vladimir Putin on the necessity of recognizing the DPR and LPR and on discussing said draft appeal."

A source told Interfax that the Council of the State Duma plans to prepare two draft resolutions dealing with the appeal to the president to recognize the Donbas self-proclaimed republics' independence to be debated at the chamber's plenary session.

Ukrainian defense minister calls Belarusian counterpart

MINSK. Feb 14 (Interfax) - Ukrainian Defense Minister Oleksiy Reznikov has called his Belarusian counterpart Viktor Khrenin, the Belarusian Defense Ministry said on Monday.

"During the phone call, the parties discussed the current state of cooperation in the military field, existing sore points, and specific steps that should be taken to improve the atmosphere of confidence and security in the region," it said.

"During the conversation, Belarusian Defense Minister Lieut. Gen. Viktor Khrenin said that the Ukrainian people have been and will continue to be brotherly people for Belarus and that Belarus is not the initiator of tensions in relations between Belarus and Ukraine," it said.

Reznikov called for resuming cooperation between the two countries and stepping up collaboration on security and mutual confidence, it said.

Ukrainian defense minister sees positive signal in phone call with Belarusian counterpart

KYIV. Feb 14 (Interfax) - Ukrainian Defense Minister Oleksiy Reznikov has spoken with his Belarusian counterpart Viktor Khrenin over the phone.

"Had a phone call with the Belarusian Defense Minister Viktor Khrenin. The goal of the dialogue was to relieve stress and prevent an escalation in relations. We discussed topical issues and determined an algorithm for further interaction," Reznikov said on Twitter on Monday

"I see this as a positive signal and the first step towards cooperation," he said.

Ukraine's interior minister urges fellow citizens not to panic over border tensions with Russia

KYIV. Feb 14 (Interfax) - Ukraine's Interior Ministry is working across its structure to ensure the country's internal security, Interior Minister Denys Monastyrskyi said, urging citizens to stay calm and continue going about their daily business.

"Some 300,000 policemen, national guardsmen, border guards and rescuers are doing their daily service of protecting Ukraine's internal security. Despite whatever claims are being made about a potential Russian aggression, no one panics and no one is afraid: everyone is simply doing their job for the peace of the Ukrainians," Monastyrskyi said in a video address uploaded on the ministry's YouTube channel.

Meanwhile, the Ukrainian armed forces, "together with diplomats and intelligence agents, are providing Ukraine's external security," he said.

The Interior Ministry will make every effort to prevent separatist manifestations similar to those which took place in Kharkiv, Luhansk, and Donetsk in the spring of 2014, the minister said.

"We will not allow a repeat of Sloviansk either," Monastyrskyi said, adding that that if someone "attempts to seize administrative buildings, he will be shot dead by our special forces without warning or hesitation."

llm_judgement.note: Different Interfax stories on the same broad crisis day but covering distinct events and quotes
